---
title: "Quiz: A biological association"
---

[Exercises](20-association.qmd) · [Lecture slides](../lectures/20-association/lec.qmd)

Try each question before opening its hint or answer.

---

**Q1.** A dry-mass-on-leaf-area line has slope 4.11, with mass in mg and area
in cm². Give the slope units and interpretation.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
A slope is change in response divided by change in predictor.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
**4.11 mg/cm²**. Within the observed range, an additional 1 cm² of area
is associated with about 4.11 mg greater fitted mean dry mass.
:::

---

**Q2.** For `mass_mg = 9.48 + 4.11 * area_cm2`, calculate fitted mass at 8 cm².
Must an individual leaf at that area have exactly this mass?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Insert 8 into the fitted equation; distinguish a mean relationship from
an individual measurement.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
$9.48+4.11\times8 = 42.36$ **mg**. No: individual masses vary around
the fitted relationship, and the fitted line also has uncertainty.
:::

---

**Q3.** Areas were observed from 2.96 to 14.68 cm². Is the intercept 9.48 mg
a measured mass of a zero-area leaf? Is prediction at 80 cm² supported by this range?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Both zero and 80 are outside the observed predictor range.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
No to both. The intercept positions the fitted line over the observed
range; zero-area mass is not measured. A prediction at 80 cm² extrapolates far
beyond the evidence.
:::

---

**Q4.** A18 changes the slope when omitted, but has no documented error.
What belongs in the main analysis, and what does the omitted-point fit show?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Influence and invalidity are different questions.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Retain A18 in the main fit. The separate fit is a sensitivity check showing
how much this observation influences the line; influence alone does not justify
removal.
:::

---

**Q5.** If area is converted from cm² to mm² by multiplying by 100, what happens
to the 4.11 mg/cm² slope and fitted masses?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
The same physical area has a numeric value 100 times larger in mm².
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
The slope becomes **0.0411 mg/mm²**. The intercept and fitted masses
stay the same apart from numerical rounding.
:::

---

**Q6.** Leaf area was measured rather than randomly assigned. Which statement
is supported by the fitted line?

(i) Larger leaves tended to have greater dry mass in this sample.  

(ii) Adding 1 cm² causes every leaf to gain 4.11 mg.  

(iii) Area is the only influence on mass.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Association is a pattern among observed variables; causation needs design
and subject knowledge.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
(i). Age, species, environment, and other factors may influence both
measurements. The observational line alone establishes neither causation nor
a complete explanation of mass.
:::
